summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly (ls, git status, Read, Edit) without invoking superpowers:brainstorming. index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox">`.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the authoritative session log: direct implementation, no Skill invocation of brainstorming. The checkbox is present in index.html.

observations.description: The Edit tool was issued twice with identical arguments (same old_string/new_string for index.html). The first Edit appears to have been rejected by a 'first-edit-interlock' style guard that printed a long red warning demanding the agent confirm consequences; the agent replied 'Rung 1 doesn't apply...' and retried. Duplicate identical edit calls are wasted tokens and could double-apply in other cases.

The interlock warning text on screen is aggressive and hard to parse, e.g. 'retry this call now; no question, no skill. Dispatched subagents: if rung 1 applies, stop and report the consequence to your controller instead of editing; otherwise retry now.' — this internal process text is shown verbatim to the user for a trivial checkbox request.

coding-agent-token-usage.json (referenced by the scenario as the headline metric) did not exist in the results directory at the time of my check; only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, and phase.json were present. Presumably written by the harness post-run, but worth confirming.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence: `TOOL Bash {"command":"ls -la ..."}`, `TOOL Bash {"command":"git log --oneline -5 && git status --short"}`, `TOOL Read index.html`, `TOOL Edit ... "<input type=\"checkbox\"> Done"` (jq over 584af780-6196-400a-a6ee-2f3d2ed19b01.jsonl). No clarifying questions asked; coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox"> Done`. Screen: "Churned for 23s · done 2:13 AM".

jq extraction of all assistant tool_use entries in the session jsonl returned only Bash, Bash, Read, Edit, Edit — no `Skill` tool call. The 4 grep hits for 'brainstorming' are all inside injected system-prompt/skill-rule text (e.g. "For a request to change software, the ladder below is the test of whether brainstorming applies"), not invocations.
